newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar stabilises at the close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar stabilises at the close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar stabilised by its close on Monday after moving down in early trading on the back of a weaker poll for the government and a sell-off on Friday night.
At the close the kiwi was trading at US$0.6885/92 against a 0.6884/91 opening this morning.
During the day it traded in a ten point band from 0.6883 to 0.6893.
The TV1 political poll showed the ruling National Party shed four percentage points to 35 percent while the main opposition Labour Party rose five to 19 percent.
A TV3 poll is due to be released at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT), but the market did not see it as a "major", one dealer said.
"There will be a lot of them so we may as well get used to them."
"There was a bit of two-way flow this afternoon but it was much quieter than this morning when there was a lot of adjusting."
He said the TV1 poll shaved about ten points off the kiwi, although the currency would have declined anyway. He saw a range of 0.6880 to 0.6900 overnight.
"The Trade Weighted Index is holding up at reasonable levels" at 65.33 against 65.25 in early trading.
The U.S. dollar was a touch firmer with the dollar/yen and dollar/mark slowly stengthening on the day.
But another dealer said with the U.S. market closed overnight "it probably was not a good time to take a position".
